# punkroc (punk)

> punkroc ("punk") is an Elm-like language on top of the Roc compiler: Elm's
> syntax, names and argument order, Roc's types, platforms and speed. Files end
> in `.punk`. This file is everything you need to write punk programs.

If you know Elm, write Elm and read the section "Differences from Elm".
Everything not listed there works as in Elm.

## Tools

The `punk` command is the Roc compiler (`zig-out/bin/punk`, also `roc`).

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `punk check --json app.punk` | Type-check without building. Problems as JSON on stdout (see "Errors"). Exit code 1 when there are errors. Fast (under a second). |
| `punk fmt app.punk ...` | Lay files out in the one canonical form. `--check` only lists files that are not formatted. |
| `punk app.punk [args]` | Build and run the app. |
| `punk test app.punk` | Run the `expect` tests in the file. |

Work in this loop: write the file, `punk fmt` it, `punk check --json` it, fix
the first problem, repeat; then run it. Fix problems from the top: a later one
is often caused by an earlier one.

## A program

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../platforms/cli/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout

main! = fn () ->
    Stdout.line! "Hello"
```

The path after `platform` is relative to the `.punk` file; it points to
`platforms/cli/main.roc` in the punkroc repository. A file is an `app`
(it has `main!`) or a `module` (see "Modules").

## Syntax

```
-- a line comment
{- a block comment -}
{-| a doc comment, before a definition -}

answer : Int                      -- type annotation, then the definition
answer = 42

add : Int -> Int -> Int           -- functions are curried, as in Elm
add = fn a, b ->                  -- a lambda: `fn` params `->` body
    a + b

inc = add 1                       -- partial application
twice = fn f, x -> f (f x)        -- application by spaces: `f a b`, never `f(a, b)`

area = fn shape ->
    case shape of                 -- `case ... of`, as in Elm
        Circle r -> 3.14 * r * r
        Rect w h -> w * h

sign = fn n ->
    if n < 0 then -1 else if n == 0 then 0 else 1
```

Indentation is significant (4 spaces per level; tabs are an error). A body
on the next line is a block: any number of `name = value` lines and then the
result. There is no `let ... in`:

```
distance = fn a, b ->
    dx = a.x - b.x
    dy = a.y - b.y
    F64.sqrt (dx * dx + dy * dy)
```

Pipelines go line by line. `x |> f a` is `f a x`: the value goes last.

```
total =
    input
        |> String.lines
        |> List.map String.trim
        |> List.filter (fn line -> not (String.isEmpty line))
        |> List.length
```

### Values

| Kind | Syntax |
|------|--------|
| numbers | `42`, `-3`, `3.14`, `0xff`, `1_000_000` |
| strings | `"text"`, interpolation `"n = ${String.fromInt n}"` (only a `Str` goes inside `${}`), `"""` multi-line `"""` |
| characters | `'a'` |
| lists | `[1, 2, 3]`, `xs ++ ys` |
| tuples | `(1, "a")`; fields `.0`, `.1`: `pair.0`, `List.map .0 pairs` |
| records | `{ name = "Ann", age = 7 }`, `person.name`, `.name` (accessor function), update `{ person | age = 8 }`, field punning `{ name, age }` |
| tags | `Red`, `Circle 2.0`, `Ok 1`, `Err (BadLine line)`, `Just x`, `Nothing` |
| unit | `()` (argument of `main!` and other effects with no input), `{}` (empty record, the result of an effect such as `Stdout.line!`) |

### Operators

`+ - * /` (`/` on floats), `//` (integer division), `%` (remainder),
`== /= < <= > >=`, `&& ||`, `not x`, `++` (lists and strings), `|>`, `<|`.
A range of numbers is `List.range 1 5` (`[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`). Dividing an
integer by zero gives 0, as in Elm.

### Types

```
type Shape = Circle Float | Rect Float Float     -- a union (custom type)

type Tree a
    = Leaf
    | Node (Tree a) a (Tree a)

type alias Point = { x : Int, y : Int }         -- a record type

parse : Str -> Result (List Int) _              -- `_`: let the compiler infer it
```

Builtin types: `Int` (64-bit, `I64`), `Float` (`F64`), `Bool` (`True`,
`False`), `Str`, `List a`, `Dict k v`, `Set a`, `Maybe a` (`Just a |
Nothing`), `Result ok err` (`Ok ok | Err err`), `Order` (`LT | EQ | GT`), and
Roc's sized numbers `U8 U16 U32 U64 I8 I16 I32 I64 F32 F64 Dec`.

Your own types, tuples, records, lists and strings support `==` and can be
`Dict` keys and `Set` members: `Dict (Int, Int) Int` is the usual grid.

### Numbers and characters

A number literal gets its type from where it is used; give a top-level
value an annotation (`total : U64`) when it matters. `Int` and `I64` are the
same type, as are `Float` and `F64`. Convert between sized numbers with the
functions of the source type:

| From to | Function |
|---------|----------|
| `U64` to `Int`, `Int` to `U64` | `toInt n`, `fromInt n` |
| always fits (`U8` to `I64`, `I32` to `I64`, ...) | `U8.toI64 b`, `I32.toI64 n` |
| may not fit | `I64.toU8Try n` (a `Result`), or `I64.toU8Wrap n` (wraps around) |
| to and from text | `I64.toStr n`, `U64.fromStr s` (a `Result`), `String.fromInt`, `String.toInt` (a `Maybe`) |

A character literal `'a'` is a number (its code). `Str.toUtf8 s` gives the
bytes of a string as `List U8`, and `'0'` compares with them, so the digit of
a byte `b` is `U8.toI64 (b - '0')`.

### Errors are tags

Errors are tags; you do not have to declare an error type. A function that can
fail returns `Result value _` and makes up the error tags it needs:
`Err (BadLine line)`. A caller matches on them or passes them on with `try`.

### Patterns

In `case`, in lambda parameters and on the left of `=`:

```
case xs of
    [] -> "empty"
    [x] -> "one"
    [first, second, ..] -> "two or more"
    [first, ..rest] -> "first and the rest"

fn (a, b) -> a + b                      -- tuple
fn { x, y } -> x + y                    -- record
case r of
    Ok n if n > 0 -> "positive"         -- guard
    Ok _ -> "not positive"
    Err (BadLine line) -> line
    Err _ -> "other error"
```

### Errors with `try`

`try` before a call that returns a `Result` unwraps an `Ok`, or returns the
`Err` from the enclosing function at once:

```
parseLine : Str -> Result (I64, I64) _
parseLine = fn line ->
    case String.split "," line of
        [a, b] -> Ok (try I64.fromStr a, try I64.fromStr b)
        _ -> Err (BadLine line)

parseAll : Str -> Result (List (I64, I64)) _
parseAll = fn text ->
    pairs =
        text
            |> String.lines
            |> try List.mapTry parseLine  -- `try` in a pipeline checks the result
    Ok pairs
```

`try` takes one call (`try f a b`); for more use parentheses:
`try (s |> String.trim |> parse)`. There is no postfix `?`.

### Loops: `fold`

There is no `var`, `for`, `while` or `return`. Use `List.map`, `List.filter`,
recursion, or `fold`:

```
fold xs into 0 with fn x, total -> total + x       -- inline form

xs |> fold into 0 with add                          -- the list from a pipe

fold x in xs into total = 0                         -- block form, one accumulator:
    total + x                                       -- the body is its new value

fold x in xs into count = 0, sum = 0                -- more accumulators: the body is a
    if x > 0 then { count = count + 1, sum = sum + x } else {}
                                                    -- record of the ones that change;
                                                    -- the fold's value is a record of all
```

### Effects

A name ending in `!` does something (prints, reads a file). Call effects only
from other `!` functions; `main!` is the start. Each effect is one line in a
block:

```
main! = fn () ->
    text = Stdin.readAll! ()
    Stdout.line! "read ${String.fromInt (String.length text)} bytes"
```

### Tests

```
expect add 1 2 == 3
```

Top-level `expect`s run with `punk test`. `crash` and `dbg` are only allowed
inside an `expect` (rules P101, P102).

### Modules

```
module Grid exposing (Grid, at, Cell(..))      -- (..) exposes the tags too

import Grid exposing (Grid, at)                -- in another file: Grid.punk next to it
import Grid                                    -- then use Grid.at
```

Everything a module exposes needs a type annotation (rule P201).

## Differences from Elm

| Elm | punk |
|-----|------|
| `\x -> x + 1` | `fn x -> x + 1`, several parameters `fn a, b -> ...` |
| `let a = 1 in a + 2` | a block: `a = 1` on one line, `a + 2` on the next |
| `String` type | `Str` (the module is still `String`: `String.split`) |
| `Int` is JS-sized | `Int` is 64-bit; `List.len`, `List.get`, `List.countIf`, `Dict.len` use `U64` (convert with `toInt` / `fromInt`) |
| `"a" ++ String.fromInt n` | works, but `"a${String.fromInt n}"` is the usual way |
| `Debug.log` | `dbg`, only inside `expect` |
| `Maybe` everywhere | Roc's functions return `Result` (`List.first`, `List.get`, `Dict.get`); the Elm-only ones return `Maybe` (`List.head`, `String.toInt`) |
| `List.filterMap` with `Maybe` | `List.filterMap` keeps the `Ok`s of a function that returns a `Result` |
| `case` on `x :: xs` | list patterns `[x, ..xs]`; `::` does not exist |
| `(+)`, `(::)` | write a lambda: `fn a, b -> a + b` |
| `Html`, `Browser`, `Cmd` | not yet; programs are command-line apps on a platform |
| `port`, `Task` | effects are `!` functions |
| `type alias Model = {...}` | same |
| `/=` | same (`!=` works too; write `/=`) |
| a module per file, `exposing` | same; the file name is the module name |

## Differences from Roc

You may know Roc. punk is Roc with Elm's surface; do not write Roc syntax:

| Roc | punk |
|-----|------|
| `\|a, b\| a + b` | `fn a, b -> a + b` |
| `f(a, b)` | `f a b` |
| `List.map(xs, f)`, `xs.map(f)` | `List.map f xs`, `xs \|> List.map f` |
| `match x { A => 1, B => 2 }` | `case x of` with `A -> 1` lines |
| `if c { a } else { b }` | `if c then a else b` |
| `x?` | `try x` |
| `List.keep_if`, snake_case | `List.filter` (Elm name) or `List.keepIf`; camelCase everywhere |
| `List.walk(xs, 0, \|s, x\| ...)` | `List.foldl (fn x, s -> ...) 0 xs`: the state comes last in the lambda |
| `Shape := [Circle(F64)]` | `type Shape = Circle F64` |
| `# comment` | `-- comment` |
| `var`, `for`, `while`, `return` | `fold`, recursion, `List.*` |

Roc functions without an Elm name exist too, in camelCase, with the value
they work on last: `Str.splitOn "," text`, `List.dropIf`, `U64.toStr n`.
Number functions keep Roc's order: `U64.toStr n`, `U64.fromStr s`,
`I64.toStr n`, `F64.toStr x`, `U64.absDiff a b`, `F64.sqrt x`.

## Errors

`punk check --json` writes one JSON document:

```
{
  "file": "app.punk",
  "errors": 1,
  "warnings": 0,
  "problems": [
    {
      "severity": "error",
      "code": "roc/name-not-in-scope",
      "title": "Name Not In Scope",
      "file": "app.punk",
      "line": 7, "column": 34, "endLine": 7, "endColumn": 44,
      "message": "Nothing is named notDefined in this scope. ...",
      "fix": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Positions are 1-based and in the `.punk` file. `code` is stable:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `P001` | punk syntax error (the message says what was expected) |
| `P101` | `crash` outside an `expect`: return a `Result` or `Maybe` instead |
| `P102` | `dbg` outside an `expect` |
| `P201` | an exposed value of a module has no type annotation |
| `P301` | the SQL of `Sql.query` is not a string literal: pass values as parameters (`$1`) |
| `P401` | a `table` declaration: its row type is not a record of storable columns, its key is not a column, or a policy line is missing |
| `P402` | a query that can't run in the database: not a pipeline from a table to `Db.all`/`first`/`update`/`delete`, or a function the database can't run |
| `P403` | a query uses a column the table doesn't have, or a value of the wrong type |
| `P404` | a query does what the table's policy forbids (`delete nobody`) |
| `roc/<title>` | a problem the type checker found, such as `roc/type-mismatch`, `roc/name-not-in-scope`, `roc/missing-method` |

Warnings (`severity: "warning"`) do not stop the program. A warning
`roc/unconditional-condition` on `main!` for a value known at compile time
(such as an example input in the file) is harmless.

Some type-checker messages mention Roc syntax (`.toStr()`, `List.len`): read
them as the punk spelling (`String.fromInt`, `List.length`).

## The platform

`platforms/cli` (`app [main!] { pf: platform "platforms/cli/main.roc" }`,
relative to your file) provides:

```
Stdout.line! : Str => {}             -- prints a line
Stdout.write! : Str => {}            -- prints without a newline
Stderr.line! : Str => {}
Stdin.line! : () => Str              -- one line, "" at the end of the input
Stdin.readAll! : () => Str
File.read! : Str => Result Str [FileErr Str]
File.write! : Str -> Str => Result {} [FileErr Str]   -- path, text
Arg.list! : () => List Str           -- the arguments after the program name
Clock.now! : () => I64               -- milliseconds since 1970 (Elm's posixToMillis)
Clock.elapsed! : () => I64           -- milliseconds since the program started
Random.u64! : () => U64              -- 64 random bits from the OS
```

`File.read!` and `File.write!` only work on files named on the command line
(`punk app.punk input.txt`); any other path gives `Err (FileErr msg)`. Take
the path from `Arg.list!`, never write a file name into the program.

Import what you use: `import pf.Stdout`, `import pf.File`, ...

### The server platform

`platforms/server` is for HTTP servers (on ambit's server platform). The app
is one function, called for every request:

```
app [handle!] { pf: platform "platforms/server/main.roc", json: "packages/json/main.roc" }

import pf.Http exposing [Request, Response]

handle! : Request => Response
handle! = fn req ->
    case req.method of
        "GET" if req.path == "/hello" -> { status = 200, headers = [], body = Str.toUtf8 "hello\n" }
        _ -> { status = 404, headers = [], body = [] }
```

```
Request : { method : Str, path : Str, query : Str, headers : List (Str, Str), body : List U8 }
Response : { status : U16, headers : List (Str, Str), body : List U8 }
Kv.get! : Str => Result (Maybe Str) [KvErr Str]
Kv.put! : Str -> Str => Result {} [KvErr Str]      -- key, value
Kv.delete! : Str => Result {} [KvErr Str]
Clock.now! : () => I64                              -- milliseconds since 1970
Random.u64! : () => U64
Config.text! : () => Str                            -- the configuration, JSON: decode it with json.Decode
Log.info! : Str => {}                               -- also Log.warn!, Log.error!
```

Header names in a request are lower case. The app has no other way to reach
the world: no files, no network, no environment. It is not run with
`punk app.punk`: `punk build` makes an archive that a small Rust crate links
and tests (see `platforms/server/README.md` and `examples/punk/shortener/`).
Annotate an effect with more arguments as `Settings -> Str => Result Response _`.

### Postgres: tables and queries

Declare a table in punk, with the type of its rows, its key and who may
read, insert, update and delete its rows (a table without all four doesn't
compile, P401). Queries are pipelines from the table; punk turns each one
into one SQL statement with parameters, and checks the columns and their
types. `punk check --schema app.punk` prints the `CREATE TABLE`.

```
import pf.Db

type alias Link =
    { id : Str
    , url : Str
    , created : Int
    }

table links : Link
    key id
    read everyone
    insert everyone
    update nobody
    delete nobody

findLink : Str -> Db.Query (Maybe Link)
findLink = fn id ->
    links
        |> Db.filter (fn link -> link.id == id)
        |> Db.first

-- in an effect: case try Db.run! (findLink id) of ...
```

```
Db.filter : (row -> Bool) -> query -> query       -- several filters: AND
Db.map : (row -> b) -> query -> query             -- .url, or a record { url = l.url, ... }
Db.all : query -> Db.Query (List row)             -- ends a query
Db.first : query -> Db.Query (Maybe row)          -- LIMIT 1
Db.insert : row -> table -> Db.Query Int          -- the number of rows changed
Db.insertIfNew : row -> table -> Db.Query Int     -- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: 0 when the key is taken
Db.update : (row -> row) -> query -> Db.Query Int -- (fn l -> { l | url = new }), after filters
Db.delete : query -> Db.Query Int
Db.run! : Db.Query a => Result a _                -- errors: PgErr { code, message }, RowErr Str
Db.toSql : Db.Query a -> Str
```

Column types: `Str`, `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, and `Maybe` of one of these
(a column that can be NULL; compare it with `== Nothing`). The functions of
`filter`, `map` and `update` are written in the query (`fn link -> ...`) and
use only the row's fields, values from outside the query (they become
parameters), `==`, `/=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `&&`, `||`, `not`, `+`, `-`,
`*` and `++`; anything else is P402: compute it before the query. `filter`
comes before `map`, and a query has at most one `map`. A table's name is not
a value: it only starts a query. For what the query language can't do yet
(joins, sorting, aggregates), write the SQL yourself with `Sql.query`:

### Postgres: SQL by hand

The database the wiring gives the app. A query is SQL written in the program
plus its parameters (`$1`, `$2`, ...); a row decoder reads the rows, as
`json.Decode` reads JSON. The SQL of `Sql.query` has to be a string literal
without `${...}` (rule P301): values always go in as parameters.

```
import pf.Postgres
import pf.Sql
import pf.Row

linkRow : Row.Decoder Link
linkRow =
    Row.map2 (fn created, url -> { created, url })
        (Row.field "created" Row.int)
        (Row.field "url" Row.text)

findLink : Str -> Sql.Query
findLink = fn id ->
    Sql.query "SELECT created, url FROM links WHERE id = $1" [Sql.text id]

-- in an effect: case try Postgres.row! linkRow (findLink id) of ...
```

```
Sql.query : Str -> List Sql.Param -> Sql.Query      -- the Str must be a literal (P301)
Sql.text : Str -> Sql.Param                        -- also Sql.int (Int), Sql.float, Sql.bool, Sql.null
Sql.nullable : (a -> Sql.Param) -> Maybe a -> Sql.Param
Row.field : Str -> Row.Column a -> Row.Decoder a   -- by column name
Row.int, Row.float, Row.text, Row.bool : Row.Column _   -- Row.nullable : Row.Column a -> Row.Column (Maybe a)
Row.map, Row.map2 ... Row.map5, Row.succeed, Row.fail, Row.andThen
Postgres.rows! : Row.Decoder a -> Sql.Query => Result (List a) _
Postgres.row! : Row.Decoder a -> Sql.Query => Result (Maybe a) _      -- more than one row is a RowErr
Postgres.execute! : Sql.Query => Result U64 _                         -- the number of rows changed
-- errors: PgErr { code : Str, message : Str } (code is the SQLSTATE, "23505" = unique violation), RowErr Str
```

Columns are read as bool, int (`int2/4/8`), float (`float4/8`) or text
(`text`, `varchar`); convert anything else in the SQL (`created::text`,
`extract(epoch from t)::int8`). A parameter must have the type the query
expects (`Sql.int` for an `integer` column). Each query commits on its own:
there are no transactions yet.

### JSON: the `json` package

Elm's `Json.Decode` and `Json.Encode`, as the modules `Decode` and `Encode`
of the package `packages/json` (add `json: "packages/json/main.roc"` to the
app header, relative to your file):

```
import json.Decode as D
import json.Encode as E

type alias Link = { url : Str, created : Int }

link : D.Decoder Link
link =
    D.map2 (fn url, created -> { url, created })
        (D.field "url" D.string)
        (D.field "created" D.int)

D.decodeString link text                    -- Result Link D.Error; D.errorToString for a message
E.encode 0 (E.object [("url", E.string l.url), ("created", E.int l.created)])
```

Decoders: `string int float bool null value list keyValuePairs field at index
maybe nullable oneOf succeed fail map map2 map3 map4 map5 andThen`. Encoders:
`string int float bool null list object dict`, and `E.encode indent value`.
There is no `andMap`: use `map2` to `map5`, or `andThen`. `Value` (`import
json.Value`) is the JSON tree; `Value.parse : Str -> Result Value Str`.
Do not compare a `Value` or a `D.Error` with `==` (the compiler hangs); compare
the encoded text instead.

## Standard library

The functions an Elm or Roc programmer reaches for first. The value a
function works on is its last argument, so they fit `|>` and partial
application.

### List

```
List.map : (a -> b) -> List a -> List b
List.filter : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> List a
List.filterMap : (before -> Result after err) -> List before -> List after
List.concatMap : (a -> List b) -> List a -> List b
List.indexedMap : (Int -> a -> b) -> List a -> List b
List.map2 : (a -> b -> c) -> List a -> List b -> List c

List.foldr : (item -> state -> state) -> state -> List item -> state
List.sum : List item -> item
List.length : List a -> Int
List.len : List item -> U64
List.isEmpty : List item -> Bool
List.head : List a -> Maybe a
List.tail : List a -> Maybe (List a)
List.first : List item -> Result item [ListWasEmpty]
List.last : List item -> Result item [ListWasEmpty]
List.get : U64 -> List item -> Result item [OutOfBounds]
List.set : U64 -> a -> List a -> Result (List a) [OutOfBounds]
List.update : U64 -> (a -> a) -> List a -> Result (List a) [OutOfBounds]
List.range : Int -> Int -> List Int
List.reverse : List item -> List item
List.sort : List item -> List item

List.take : Int -> List a -> List a

List.all : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> Bool
List.member : a -> List a -> Bool
List.countIf : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> U64
List.dropIf : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> List a
List.findFirst : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> Result a [NotFound]

List.append : a -> List a -> List a
List.concat : List item -> List item -> List item
List.join : List (List item) -> List item
List.maximum : List a -> Maybe a

List.singleton : a -> List a
List.repeat : U64 -> a -> List a

```

### Tuple

```
Tuple.first : (a, b) -> a
Tuple.second : (a, b) -> b
Tuple.pair : a -> b -> (a, b)
Tuple.mapFirst : (a -> x) -> (a, b) -> (x, b)
Tuple.mapSecond : (b -> y) -> (a, b) -> (a, y)
```

### Dict

```
Dict.empty : Dict k v
Dict.insert : k -> v -> Dict k v -> Dict k v
Dict.get : k -> Dict k v -> Result v [KeyNotFound]
Dict.update : k -> (Result v [Missing] -> Result v [Missing]) -> Dict k v -> Dict k v
Dict.remove : k -> Dict k v -> Dict k v
Dict.contains : k -> Dict k v -> Bool
Dict.keys : Dict k v -> List k
Dict.values : Dict k v -> List v
Dict.toList : Dict k v -> List (k, v)
Dict.fromList : List (k, v) -> Dict k v
Dict.fold : (k -> v -> state -> state) -> state -> Dict k v -> state
Dict.map : (k -> a -> b) -> Dict k a -> Dict k b
Dict.keepIf : ((k, v) -> Bool) -> Dict k v -> Dict k v
Dict.len : Dict k v -> U64
```

## Cookbook

### Read a file given on the command line, solve, print

The shape of an Advent of Code solution: the example input in the file, the
real input from a file argument. (The cookbook files live in
`examples/punk/aoc2024/`, hence their longer platform path; some use the
`test/fx/platform` test platform, which has `Stdout` too. Use
`platforms/cli` for your own programs.)

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/cli/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout
import pf.File
import pf.Arg

{-| Advent of Code 2024, day 1: Historian Hysteria.

Without arguments it solves the example; `roc Day01.punk input.txt` solves
your own puzzle input.
-}

example =
    """
    3   4
    4   3
    2   5
    1   3
    3   9
    3   3
    """

main! = fn () ->
    case Arg.list! () of
        [path] ->
            case File.read! path of
                Ok input -> solve! (String.trim input)
                Err (FileErr msg) -> Stdout.line! msg
        _ ->
            solve! example

solve! = fn input ->
    case parse input of
        Ok (left, right) ->
            Stdout.line! "Part 1: ${U64.toStr (part1 left right)}"
            Stdout.line! "Part 2: ${U64.toStr (part2 left right)}"
        Err _ ->
            Stdout.line! "could not parse the input"

parse : Str -> Result (List U64, List U64) _
parse = fn input ->
    pairs =
        input
            |> Str.splitOn "\n"
            |> try List.mapTry parseLine
    Ok (List.map .0 pairs, List.map .1 pairs)

parseLine : Str -> Result (U64, U64) _
parseLine = fn line ->
    case line |> Str.splitOn " " |> List.dropIf Str.isEmpty of
        [a, b] -> Ok (try U64.fromStr a, try U64.fromStr b)
        _ -> Err (BadLine line)

part1 : List U64 -> List U64 -> U64
part1 = fn left, right ->
    List.map2 distance (List.sort left) (List.sort right)
        |> List.sum

distance : U64 -> U64 -> U64
distance = fn a, b ->
    U64.absDiff a b

part2 : List U64 -> List U64 -> U64
part2 = fn left, right ->
    left
        |> List.map (fn n -> n * List.countIf (fn m -> m == n) right)
        |> List.sum
```

### A grid: `Dict (Int, Int) a`, neighbours, recursion

Written by an agent that had only this file, on the first try.

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/cli/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout
import pf.File
import pf.Arg

{-| Advent of Code 2024, day 10: Hoof It.

Without arguments it solves the example; `roc Day10.punk input.txt` solves
your own puzzle input.
-}

example =
    """
    89010123
    78121874
    87430965
    96549874
    45678903
    32019012
    01329801
    10456732
    """

main! = fn () ->
    case Arg.list! () of
        [path] ->
            case File.read! path of
                Ok input -> solve! (String.trim input)
                Err (FileErr msg) -> Stdout.line! msg
        _ ->
            solve! example

solve! = fn input ->
    grid = parse input
    heads = trailheads grid
    Stdout.line! "Part 1: ${String.fromInt (part1 grid heads)}"
    Stdout.line! "Part 2: ${String.fromInt (part2 grid heads)}"

parse : Str -> Dict (Int, Int) Int
parse = fn input ->
    input
        |> String.lines
        |> List.indexedMap (fn r, line -> parseRow r (String.trim line))
        |> List.join
        |> Dict.fromList

parseRow : Int -> Str -> List ((Int, Int), Int)
parseRow = fn r, line ->
    line
        |> Str.toUtf8
        |> List.indexedMap (fn c, b -> ((r, c), U8.toI64 b - 48))

trailheads : Dict (Int, Int) Int -> List (Int, Int)
trailheads = fn grid ->
    grid
        |> Dict.toList
        |> List.filter (fn (_, h) -> h == 0)
        |> List.map .0

heightAt : (Int, Int) -> Dict (Int, Int) Int -> Int
heightAt = fn pos, grid ->
    case Dict.get pos grid of
        Ok h -> h
        Err _ -> -1

ends : Dict (Int, Int) Int -> Int -> (Int, Int) -> List (Int, Int)
ends = fn grid, h, (r, c) ->
    if h == 9 then
        [(r, c)]
    else
        [(r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)]
            |> List.filter (fn p -> heightAt p grid == h + 1)
            |> List.concatMap (ends grid (h + 1))

part1 : Dict (Int, Int) Int -> List (Int, Int) -> Int
part1 = fn grid, heads ->
    heads
        |> List.map (fn p -> toInt (Set.len (Set.fromList (ends grid 0 p))))
        |> List.sum

part2 : Dict (Int, Int) Int -> List (Int, Int) -> Int
part2 = fn grid, heads ->
    heads
        |> List.map (fn p -> List.length (ends grid 0 p))
        |> List.sum
```

### Folds

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../test/fx/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout

{-| Folds without loops: the `fold` keyword, inline and as a block.
See src/punk/README.md, "Folds instead of loops".
-}

type Instr
    = Mul U64 U64
    | Do
    | Dont

main! = fn () ->
    numbers = [3, 9, 4, 9, 1]
    Stdout.line! "som: ${U64.toStr (som numbers)}"
    Stdout.line! "som (blok): ${U64.toStr (somBlok numbers)}"
    best = maxIndex numbers
    Stdout.line! "max: ${U64.toStr best.bestX} op index ${U64.toStr best.bestI}"
    instrs = [Mul 2 4, Dont, Mul 5 5, Mul 11 8, Do, Mul 8 5]
    Stdout.line! "aan/uit: ${U64.toStr (run instrs)}"
    Stdout.line! "met step: ${U64.toStr (runStep instrs)}"
    Stdout.line! "gemiddelde: ${U64.toStr (gemiddelde numbers)}"

som : List U64 -> U64
som = fn xs ->
    fold xs into 0 with fn x, total -> total + x

somBlok : List U64 -> U64
somBlok = fn xs ->
    fold x in xs into total = 0
        total + x

-- The first one wins when two are equal
maxIndex = fn xs ->
    fold (i, x) in List.mapWithIndex (fn x, i -> (i, x)) xs into bestI = 0, bestX = 0
        if x > bestX then { bestI = i, bestX = x } else {}

-- AoC 2024 day 3, part 2: only a Mul after a Do counts
run : List Instr -> U64
run = fn instrs ->
    result =
        fold instr in instrs into on = True, total = 0
            case instr of
                Do -> { on = True }
                Dont -> { on = False }
                Mul a b -> if on then { total = total + a * b } else {}
    result.total

-- The same with a named step, as in Elm's `update msg model`
runStep : List Instr -> U64
runStep = fn instrs ->
    instrs
        |> fold into { on = True, total = 0 } with step
        |> .total

step = fn instr, s ->
    case instr of
        Do -> { s | on = True }
        Dont -> { s | on = False }
        Mul a b -> if s.on then { s | total = s.total + a * b } else s

gemiddelde : List U64 -> U64
gemiddelde = fn xs ->
    s =
        fold x in xs into total = 0, count = 0
            { total = total + x, count = count + 1 }
    s.total // s.count
```

### Elm's names

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../test/fx/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout

{-| Elm's names in punkroc: List, Tuple, Maybe, String, compare and Int. -}

main! = fn () ->
    Stdout.line! "range: ${Str.inspect (List.range 1 5)}"
    Stdout.line! "head: ${showMaybe (List.head [3, 4])}, of []: ${showMaybe (List.head [])}"
    Stdout.line! "filter: ${Str.inspect (List.filter (fn n -> n > 2) [1, 2, 3, 4])}"
    Stdout.line! "indexedMap: ${Str.inspect (List.indexedMap (fn i, w -> "${String.fromInt i}=${w}") ["a", "b"])}"
    Stdout.line! "foldl: ${String.fromInt (List.foldl (fn x, acc -> acc * 10 + x) 0 [1, 2, 3])}"
    Stdout.line! "foldr: ${String.fromInt (List.foldr (fn x, acc -> acc * 10 + x) 0 [1, 2, 3])}"
    Stdout.line! "tuple: ${Tuple.first ("x", 1)} ${String.fromInt (Tuple.second ("x", 1))}"
    Stdout.line! "sortWith: ${Str.inspect (List.sortWith (fn a, b -> compare b a) [2, 3, 1])}"
    Stdout.line! "length: ${String.fromInt (List.length [1, 2, 3] - 5)}"
    Stdout.line! "toInt: ${String.fromInt (toInt (List.len [1, 2]) - 3)}"
    Stdout.line! "words: ${String.join "|" (String.words "  een twee  drie ")}"
    Stdout.line! "toInt: ${showMaybe (String.toInt "42")} ${showMaybe (String.toInt "x")}"
    Stdout.line! "default: ${String.fromInt (Maybe.withDefault 0 (List.maximum [4, 9, 2]))}"

showMaybe : Maybe Int -> Str
showMaybe = fn m ->
    case m of
        Just n -> "Just ${String.fromInt n}"
        Nothing -> "Nothing"
```

### Standard input and files

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/cli/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout
import pf.Stdin
import pf.File
import pf.Arg

{-| punkroc's platform: the command line, files and standard input. -}

main! = fn () ->
    case Arg.list! () of
        [path] ->
            case File.read! path of
                Ok text -> report! "${path}" text
                Err (FileErr msg) -> Stdout.line! msg
        _ ->
            report! "stdin" (Stdin.readAll! ())

report! = fn name, text ->
    lines = String.lines (String.trim text)
    Stdout.line! "${name}: ${String.fromInt (List.length lines)} lines"
    Stdout.line! "first: ${Maybe.withDefault "" (List.head lines)}"
```

### JSON decoders and encoders

```
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/cli/main.roc", json: "../../../packages/json/main.roc" }

import pf.Stdout
import json.Value
import json.Decode as D
import json.Encode as E

{-| JSON with the `json` package: Elm-style decoders and encoders, written by hand. -}

type alias User =
    { name : Str
    , age : Int
    , email : Maybe Str
    , tags : List Str
    }

user : D.Decoder User
user =
    D.map4 (fn name, age, email, tags -> { name, age, email, tags })
        (D.field "name" D.string)
        (D.field "age" D.int)
        (D.maybe (D.field "email" D.string))
        (D.oneOf [D.field "tags" (D.list D.string), D.succeed []])

encodeUser : User -> Value
encodeUser = fn u ->
    E.object
        [ ("name", E.string u.name)
        , ("age", E.int u.age)
        , ("email", Maybe.withDefault E.null (Maybe.map E.string u.email))
        , ("tags", E.list E.string u.tags)
        ]

type Shape
    = Circle Float
    | Rect Float Float

-- A union: the "kind" field says which fields follow.
shape : D.Decoder Shape
shape =
    D.field "kind" D.string
        |> D.andThen
            (fn kind ->
                case kind of
                    "circle" -> D.map (fn r -> Circle r) (D.field "r" D.float)
                    "rect" -> D.map2 (fn w, h -> Rect w h) (D.field "w" D.float) (D.field "h" D.float)
                    _ -> D.fail "unknown kind ${kind}"
            )

area : Shape -> Float
area = fn s ->
    case s of
        Circle r -> 3.0 * r * r
        Rect w h -> w * h

roundTrip : Int -> Str -> Str
roundTrip = fn indent, text ->
    case Value.parse text of
        Ok v -> Value.encode indent v
        Err problem -> "error: ${problem}"

show : Result a D.Error -> (a -> Str) -> Str
show = fn result, f ->
    case result of
        Ok x -> f x
        Err e -> "error: ${D.errorToString e}"

inputs : List Str
inputs =
    [ "{\"name\": \"Ann\", \"age\": 7, \"email\": \"ann@example.com\", \"tags\": [\"a\", \"b\"]}"
    , "{\"name\": \"Bob\", \"age\": 40}"
    , "{\"name\": \"Cy\", \"age\": \"old\"}"
    , "{\"name\": \"Di\", \"age\": 1.5}"
    , "[1, 2"
    , "{\"name\": \"Ed\", \"age\": 3, \"tags\": [\"x\", 4]}"
    ]

main! = fn () ->
    Stdout.line! "-- users"
    inputs
        |> List.map (fn text -> show (D.decodeString user text) (fn u -> E.encode 0 (encodeUser u)))
        |> List.forEach! Stdout.line!

    Stdout.line! "-- shapes"
    [ "{\"kind\": \"circle\", \"r\": 2}"
    , "{\"kind\": \"rect\", \"w\": 2, \"h\": 3.5}"
    , "{\"kind\": \"star\"}"
    ]
        |> List.map (fn text -> show (D.decodeString shape text) (fn s -> F64.toStr (area s)))
        |> List.forEach! Stdout.line!

    Stdout.line! "-- text"
    -- Escapes and characters beyond ASCII survive a round trip.
    tricky = "  {\"s\": \"tab\\there \\\"quoted\\\" \\u00e9 \\ud83d\\ude00\", \"n\": -0.5e-3, \"empty\": [], \"o\": {}}  "
    Stdout.line! (roundTrip 0 tricky)
    Stdout.line! (roundTrip 4 tricky)

    -- Bad JSON says what is wrong, and where.
    ["", "nul", "01", "1.", "\"no end", "{\"a\" 1}", "[1,]", "\"\\x\"", "1 2"]
        |> List.map (fn text -> "${E.encode 0 (E.string text)} -> ${roundTrip 0 text}")
        |> List.forEach! Stdout.line!

    Stdout.line! "-- at, index, keyValuePairs, nullable"
    nested = "{\"user\": {\"names\": [\"first\", \"second\"]}, \"counts\": {\"a\": 1, \"b\": 2}, \"x\": null}"
    Stdout.line! (show (D.decodeString (D.at ["user", "names"] (D.index 1 D.string)) nested) (fn s -> s))
    Stdout.line! (show (D.decodeString (D.field "counts" (D.keyValuePairs D.int)) nested) (fn kvs -> kvs |> List.map (fn (k, v) -> "${k}=${String.fromInt v}") |> Str.joinWith ","))
    Stdout.line! (show (D.decodeString (D.field "x" (D.nullable D.int)) nested) (fn m -> Maybe.withDefault "null" (Maybe.map String.fromInt m)))
    Stdout.line! (show (D.decodeString (D.at ["user", "names"] (D.index 5 D.string)) nested) (fn s -> s))
    Stdout.line! (show (D.decodeString (D.field "tags" (D.list D.string)) "{\"tags\": [\"x\", 4]}") (Str.joinWith ","))

-- Compared as text or as a Maybe: `==` on a type that holds itself (Value, D.Error)
-- makes the compiler hang for now.
expect Result.map (Value.encode 0) (Value.parse " [true , false,null] ") == Ok "[true,false,null]"

expect Result.toMaybe (D.decodeString (D.list D.int) "[1, 2, 3]") == Just [1, 2, 3]

expect E.encode 0 (E.float 1.5) == "1.5"
```

### A server: ambit's link shortener

```
app [handle!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/server/main.roc", json: "../../../packages/json/main.roc" }

import pf.Http exposing [Request, Response]
import pf.Clock
import pf.Random
import pf.Kv
import pf.Config
import pf.Log
import json.Decode as D
import json.Encode as E

{-| A link shortener: ambit's `apps/shortener`, in punk.

- `POST /links` with a URL as body: creates a short link, 201 with the short URL.
- `GET /<id>`: 302 to the URL, 404 if unknown, 410 once expired.

The app can only do what the platform hands it: a clock, randomness, a
key-value store, its configuration and a log.
-}

-- Configuration, from the wiring: `{"baseUrl": "https://s.test", "ttlSeconds": 3600}`
type alias Settings =
    { baseUrl : Str
    , ttlSeconds : Int
    }

settings : D.Decoder Settings
settings =
    D.map2 (fn baseUrl, ttlSeconds -> { baseUrl, ttlSeconds })
        (D.field "baseUrl" D.string)
        (D.field "ttlSeconds" D.int)

-- A stored link: `{"created": 1700000000, "url": "https://example.com"}`
type alias Link =
    { created : Int
    , url : Str
    }

linkDecoder : D.Decoder Link
linkDecoder =
    D.map2 (fn created, url -> { created, url })
        (D.field "created" D.int)
        (D.field "url" D.string)

encodeLink : Link -> Str
encodeLink = fn link ->
    E.object
        [ ("created", E.int link.created)
        , ("url", E.string link.url)
        ]
        |> E.encode 0

maxUrl : U64
maxUrl = 2048

idLength : Int
idLength = 7

idAttempts : Int
idAttempts = 5

handle! : Request => Response
handle! = fn req ->
    case D.decodeString settings (Config.text! ()) of
        Err problem ->
            Log.error! "bad configuration: ${D.errorToString problem}"
            text 500 "bad configuration\n"
        Ok config ->
            id = Str.dropPrefix "/" req.path
            result =
                case req.method of
                    "POST" if req.path == "/links" -> create! config req.body
                    "GET" if isId id -> resolve! config id
                    _ -> Ok (text 404 "not found\n")
            case result of
                Ok response -> response
                Err (KvErr message) ->
                    Log.error! "storage failed: ${message}"
                    text 503 "storage unavailable\n"

create! : Settings -> List U8 => Result Response _
create! = fn config, body ->
    case validUrl body of
        Nothing -> Ok (text 400 "body must be an http(s) URL\n")
        Just url ->
            case try store! url idAttempts of
                Nothing -> Ok (text 503 "no free id, try again\n")
                Just id ->
                    Log.info! "link created: ${id}"
                    short = "${config.baseUrl}/${id}"
                    Ok (withHeader "location" short (text 201 "${short}\n"))

resolve! : Settings -> Str => Result Response _
resolve! = fn config, id ->
    stored = try Kv.get! (key id)
    link =
        stored
            |> Maybe.andThen (fn json -> Result.toMaybe (D.decodeString linkDecoder json))
    case link of
        Nothing -> Ok (text 404 "not found\n")
        Just { created, url } ->
            if unixSeconds (Clock.now! ()) >= created + config.ttlSeconds then
                Ok (text 410 "expired\n")
            else
                -- The URL was checked to be a valid header value when it was stored.
                Ok (withHeader "location" url (text 302 ""))

-- Stores the URL under a fresh id; `Nothing` when no free id was found.
store! : Str -> Int => Result (Maybe Str) _
store! = fn url, attemptsLeft ->
    if attemptsLeft <= 0 then
        Ok Nothing
    else
        id = newId (Random.u64! ())
        case try Kv.get! (key id) of
            Just _ -> store! url (attemptsLeft - 1)
            Nothing ->
                link = { created = unixSeconds (Clock.now! ()), url }
                try Kv.put! (key id) (encodeLink link)
                Ok (Just id)

alphabet : List U8
alphabet =
    Str.toUtf8 "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

-- Seven characters from the alphabet, the lowest digits of `n` in base 62 first.
newId : U64 -> Str
newId = fn n ->
    idChars n idLength []
        |> Str.fromUtf8
        |> Result.withDefault ""

idChars : U64 -> Int -> List U8 -> List U8
idChars = fn n, left, chars ->
    if left <= 0 then
        chars
    else
        char =
            alphabet
                |> List.get (n % 62)
                |> Result.withDefault '0'
        idChars (n // 62) (left - 1) (List.append char chars)

isId : Str -> Bool
isId = fn s ->
    bytes = Str.toUtf8 s
    List.length bytes == idLength && List.all isAlphanumeric bytes

isAlphanumeric : U8 -> Bool
isAlphanumeric = fn b ->
    (b >= '0' && b <= '9') || (b >= 'A' && b <= 'Z') || (b >= 'a' && b <= 'z')

key : Str -> Str
key = fn id ->
    "link/${id}"

-- An http(s) URL that fits in a header: no line breaks, nothing outside printable ASCII.
validUrl : List U8 -> Maybe Str
validUrl = fn body ->
    case Str.fromUtf8 body of
        Err _ -> Nothing
        Ok raw ->
            url = String.trim raw
            bytes = Str.toUtf8 url
            fits = List.len bytes <= maxUrl && List.all isHeaderByte bytes
            web = String.startsWith "https://" url || String.startsWith "http://" url
            if fits && web then Just url else Nothing

isHeaderByte : U8 -> Bool
isHeaderByte = fn b ->
    (b >= 32 && b < 127) || b == '\t'

unixSeconds : I64 -> Int
unixSeconds = fn millis ->
    millis // 1000

text : U16 -> Str -> Response
text = fn status, body ->
    { status
    , headers = [("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")]
    , body = Str.toUtf8 body
    }

withHeader : Str -> Str -> Response -> Response
withHeader = fn name, value, response ->
    { response | headers = List.append (name, value) response.headers }
```

### The same shortener with its links in Postgres

```
app [handle!] { pf: platform "../../../platforms/server/main.roc", json: "../../../packages/json/main.roc" }

import pf.Http exposing [Request, Response]
import pf.Clock
import pf.Random
import pf.Db
import pf.Config
import pf.Log
import json.Decode as D

{-| A link shortener: ambit's `apps/shortener`, in punk, with its links in
Postgres instead of a key-value store. The table and its queries are written
in punk's query language: punk turns each query into one SQL statement, and
`punk check --schema` gives the table's `CREATE TABLE` (`schema.sql`).

- `POST /links` with a URL as body: creates a short link, 201 with the short URL.
- `GET /<id>`: 302 to the URL, 404 if unknown, 410 once expired.

The app can only do what the platform hands it: a clock, randomness, a
database, its configuration and a log. Which database is up to the wiring.
-}

-- Configuration, from the wiring: `{"baseUrl": "https://s.test", "ttlSeconds": 3600}`
type alias Settings =
    { baseUrl : Str
    , ttlSeconds : Int
    }

settings : D.Decoder Settings
settings =
    D.map2 (fn baseUrl, ttlSeconds -> { baseUrl, ttlSeconds })
        (D.field "baseUrl" D.string)
        (D.field "ttlSeconds" D.int)

-- A stored link: a row of the table `links`.
type alias Link =
    { id : Str
    , url : Str
    , created : Int
    }

-- The links, one row each. Anyone may look a link up or make one; nobody
-- changes or removes one.
table links : Link
    key id
    read everyone
    insert everyone
    update nobody
    delete nobody

findLink : Str -> Db.Query (Maybe Link)
findLink = fn id ->
    links
        |> Db.filter (fn link -> link.id == id)
        |> Db.first

-- Inserts the link, unless its id is taken: then it changes no row.
insertLink : Link -> Db.Query Int
insertLink = fn link ->
    Db.insertIfNew link links

maxUrl : U64
maxUrl = 2048

idLength : Int
idLength = 7

idAttempts : Int
idAttempts = 5

handle! : Request => Response
handle! = fn req ->
    case D.decodeString settings (Config.text! ()) of
        Err problem ->
            Log.error! "bad configuration: ${D.errorToString problem}"
            text 500 "bad configuration\n"
        Ok config ->
            id = Str.dropPrefix "/" req.path
            result =
                case req.method of
                    "POST" if req.path == "/links" -> create! config req.body
                    "GET" if isId id -> resolve! config id
                    _ -> Ok (text 404 "not found\n")
            case result of
                Ok response -> response
                Err (PgErr problem) ->
                    Log.error! "storage failed (${problem.code}): ${problem.message}"
                    text 503 "storage unavailable\n"
                Err (RowErr problem) ->
                    Log.error! "a stored link doesn't fit: ${problem}"
                    text 500 "internal error\n"

create! : Settings -> List U8 => Result Response _
create! = fn config, body ->
    case validUrl body of
        Nothing -> Ok (text 400 "body must be an http(s) URL\n")
        Just url ->
            case try store! url idAttempts of
                Nothing -> Ok (text 503 "no free id, try again\n")
                Just id ->
                    Log.info! "link created: ${id}"
                    short = "${config.baseUrl}/${id}"
                    Ok (withHeader "location" short (text 201 "${short}\n"))

resolve! : Settings -> Str => Result Response _
resolve! = fn config, id ->
    case try Db.run! (findLink id) of
        Nothing -> Ok (text 404 "not found\n")
        Just link ->
            if unixSeconds (Clock.now! ()) >= link.created + config.ttlSeconds then
                Ok (text 410 "expired\n")
            else
                -- The URL was checked to be a valid header value when it was stored.
                Ok (withHeader "location" link.url (text 302 ""))

-- Stores the URL under a fresh id; `Nothing` when no free id was found.
store! : Str -> Int => Result (Maybe Str) _
store! = fn url, attemptsLeft ->
    if attemptsLeft <= 0 then
        Ok Nothing
    else
        id = newId (Random.u64! ())
        link = { id, url, created = unixSeconds (Clock.now! ()) }
        inserted = try Db.run! (insertLink link)
        if inserted == 0 then
            store! url (attemptsLeft - 1)
        else
            Ok (Just id)

alphabet : List U8
alphabet =
    Str.toUtf8 "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

-- Seven characters from the alphabet, the lowest digits of `n` in base 62 first.
newId : U64 -> Str
newId = fn n ->
    idChars n idLength []
        |> Str.fromUtf8
        |> Result.withDefault ""

idChars : U64 -> Int -> List U8 -> List U8
idChars = fn n, left, chars ->
    if left <= 0 then
        chars
    else
        char =
            alphabet
                |> List.get (n % 62)
                |> Result.withDefault '0'
        idChars (n // 62) (left - 1) (List.append char chars)

isId : Str -> Bool
isId = fn s ->
    bytes = Str.toUtf8 s
    List.length bytes == idLength && List.all isAlphanumeric bytes

isAlphanumeric : U8 -> Bool
isAlphanumeric = fn b ->
    (b >= '0' && b <= '9') || (b >= 'A' && b <= 'Z') || (b >= 'a' && b <= 'z')

-- An http(s) URL that fits in a header: no line breaks, nothing outside printable ASCII.
validUrl : List U8 -> Maybe Str
validUrl = fn body ->
    case Str.fromUtf8 body of
        Err _ -> Nothing
        Ok raw ->
            url = String.trim raw
            bytes = Str.toUtf8 url
            fits = List.len bytes <= maxUrl && List.all isHeaderByte bytes
            web = String.startsWith "https://" url || String.startsWith "http://" url
            if fits && web then Just url else Nothing

isHeaderByte : U8 -> Bool
isHeaderByte = fn b ->
    (b >= 32 && b < 127) || b == '\t'

unixSeconds : I64 -> Int
unixSeconds = fn millis ->
    millis // 1000

text : U16 -> Str -> Response
text = fn status, body ->
    { status
    , headers = [("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")]
    , body = Str.toUtf8 body
    }

withHeader : Str -> Str -> Response -> Response
withHeader = fn name, value, response ->
    { response | headers = List.append (name, value) response.headers }
```

## Style

- `punk fmt` decides the layout; do not fight it.
- Annotate every top-level function.
- Prefer pipelines over nested calls, `case` over nested `if`, and Elm's
  names (`List.filter`, `String.split`, `Maybe`) where they exist.
- Return `Result` with made-up error tags instead of crashing.
- One way to do a thing: `fold` or `List.*` for loops, `try` for errors.
